subject: [PATCH v6 02/12] mm: add PMD swap entry detection support

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David (Arm) noted that migration entries use a dedicated migratetype and suggested renaming the _swp_ part to indicate it's for softdirty entries, not just swap entries.

The reviewer noted that the patch's logic for handling softleaf entries would work without any issues, but suggested extending mm/debug_vm_pgtable.c to test PMD swap exclusive entries separately.

Reviewer David asked Usama Arif to reconsider the approach of adding PMD swap entry detection support, suggesting it would be better to create a single patch for each architecture that directly targets arch maintainers instead of competing with Kiryll's series.

Reviewer David (Arm) suggested simplifying the code by unconditionally clearing the exclusive and uffd flags in pmd_swp_clear_uffd() and pmd_swp_clear_exclusive(), eliminating unnecessary conditionals.

Reviewer David requested removal of a comment from the code, stating it is 'as clear as it gets' and can be understood directly from the surrounding code.
reviews.raw_body:
Ah, for migration entries we still use a dedicated migratetype. I actually have
on my todo list to move to PTE bits as well.

(likely the _swp_ part should then be renamed to indicate that this is for
softdirty entries, not just swap entries)

---

No softleaf implies to migration and no swap, so this would work.

You should extend mm/debug_vm_pgtable.c in a separate commit to test what
pte_swap_exclusive_tests() tests for PMDs.

---

I'm sorry for asking you to compete with Kiryll's series by creating one patch
for each architecture that directly jumps at arch maintainers :)

[...]

---

Can't we just unconditionally clear these flags?

pmd = pmd_swp_clear_uffd(pmd);
pmd = pmd_swp_clear_exclusive(pmd);

Avoids these rather unnecessary conditionals unless I am missing something.

---

Can we just drop that comment? I mean, it's as clear as it gets in the code
immediately below :)

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary:
The reviewer notes that the patch adds PMD-level swap entry support, but it was previously implemented in a 'hacked' manner across various architectures.

Reviewer noted that PMD swap entries are also softleaf entries and requested someone to resolve the overlap between swap and softleaf infrastructure.
reviews.raw_body:
We do seem to have rather hacked in PMD level stuff across the board
previously :)

---

BTW one thing I should maybe mention here is that I never quite _finished_
the softleaf thing, so there's some awkward overlap between swap stuff and
softleaf stuff (swap entries _are_ softleaf entries, just a specific kind).

Infinite TODO list etc. (maybe this is a hint/nudge to somebody else to do
it ;)

2026-08-18.patch_summary: This patch adds support for detecting PMD swap entries in the Linux kernel. When a huge page (THP) is swapped out, it's currently split into smaller PTE-level swap entries. However, to preserve huge page information across swap cycles, later patches will install a single PMD-level swap entry instead. This patch introduces infrastructure to detect these PMD swap entries and provides helper functions for architectures that support them. The changes include adding new helpers for setting and clearing the exclusive overlay bit in PMD swap entries, as well as updating softleaf layer functions to recognize and handle PMD swap entries correctly.
